entries.description: Returns inactive or cancelled accounts whose data-retention window has expired but which the pre-deletion-notice gate is refusing to hard-delete, because at least one of the 30-day and 7-day notices promised by the privacy policy was never recorded. What is blocked is the retention sweep, and only it: the notice queries select only users whose retention clock has not yet run out, so no existing path can send the missing notice and the retention sweep will hold these accounts indefinitely. A user-requested GDPR erasure is a separate authorisation and still deletes them normally; requesting deletion also removes the account from this listing. This is a read-only view — it sends nothing, extends no retention clock and waives no notice; choosing between those remedies is an open decision and will land as its own endpoint. has_email_on_file is reported per account because it is the one withholding reason the retention_deletions_withheld metric cannot separate. No email address is returned. withheld_total and the returned page come from two separate queries and are eventually consistent: a notice marker, a deletion request or a retention clock crossing the current instant between them can make the total disagree with the page by any number of rows — the gap is not bounded. as_of is when the response was calculated, after both queries returned. responseBody.name: quarantine_reason
responseBody.description: Why the rule is broken. Fixed vocabulary, never user content. Four values are in the ENFORCEMENT CLASS — the rule cannot be evaluated honestly as written, and while quarantine enforcement is on (RULE_QUARANTINE_ENFORCE, default on) the server refuses it and quarantined is true: no_conditions_matches_everything, invalid_condition_logic_defaults_to_and, unnormalizable_condition, uncoercible_condition_value. With enforcement OFF those same rules RUN and quarantined is false — nothing about them was repaired. The fifth, invalid_condition_value_shape, is never enforced in either state: a condition value of the wrong type whose intended reading is unambiguous, coerced at read time only, so the rule keeps running. Read quarantined, not this field, for whether the server is currently stopping the rule — and read enabled too, which both fields ignore entirely. The stored rule is never rewritten; edit it to make the repair permanent.

responseBody.name: quarantined
responseBody.description: True when the server is CURRENTLY preventing this rule from matching anything: it is refused before any condition is evaluated, so it applies to nothing. This is a statement about right now, not about the rule's shape. It is FALSE whenever quarantine enforcement is disabled server-wide (RULE_QUARANTINE_ENFORCE, default on), because the engine then runs the rule despite its problem. So false WITH a quarantine_reason does NOT mean the rule is healthy or that the server repaired it — it means quarantine is not what is stopping it: either the problem is one the server repairs at read time (a wrong-typed condition value with one honest reading is coerced), or enforcement is off and the rule is running exactly as written, in which case a rule with no conditions matches EVERY transaction. ⚠ This field says nothing about enabled: a disabled rule matches nothing regardless, because the engine returns early on the enabled flag before quarantine is consulted. Read enabled AND NOT quarantined for the question is the server letting this rule run — which is not the same as is it matching, because a condition the engine cannot evaluate still fails at evaluation time. Computed per request; never persisted.

responseBody.description: Optimistic-concurrency token. Incremented by user-facing updates only; background bookkeeping such as the match counter deliberately does not move it, so an ordinary sync cannot make your save look like a conflict.

So false WITH a quarantine_reason does NOT mean the rule is healthy or that the server repaired it — it means quarantine is not what is stopping it: either the problem is one the server repairs at read time (a wrong-typed condition value with one honest reading is coerced), or enforcement is off and the rule is running exactly as written, in which case a rule with no conditions matches EVERY transaction. ⚠ This field says nothing about enabled: a disabled rule matches nothing regardless, because the engine returns early on the enabled flag before quarantine is consulted. Retrieves the before/after record of every change to a transaction's category, review state or tags for the authenticated user, newest first. A row exists for each write that actually changed a tracked value; re-writing the identical value records nothing. Changes made to a transaction that has since been removed are still returned.

`change_source` answers *what was asked for*, and has five values. Two are the user acting on their own transaction: 'category' — a recategorisation, which ALSO rewrites `reviewed`/`reviewed_at` as a side effect, so a review timestamp can be lost by a write the user thought was only about the category; and 'review' — a review-state write, single or bulk, which leaves the category alone. 'tags' is a whole-array tag replace: every tag dropped is gone the moment it returns and the previous set survives nowhere else, so `prior_tags` here is the only record of it; category fields are unchanged on these rows by construction.

The remaining two record changes the user did NOT ask for, which is exactly why they are not filed under 'category'. 'settlement' is written when a pending charge posts and the sync carries the manual category from the pending row onto the posted twin, replacing whatever the twin had — it explains why the twin no longer agrees with the rule_execution_history entry for the rule that categorised it moments earlier. 'erasure' is the one source whose cause is another user: when a different user exercises GDPR erasure their custom categories are hard-deleted, and a surviving user's transaction pointing at one has its override cleared. That row is the ONLY explanation anywhere for a category changing under a user who did nothing — no other record of it exists, and none is written for the erased user's own transactions, which are deleted in the same database transaction.

requestBody.description: Actual amount transferred

entries.description: Releases the fuzzy-match reservation on a pending/accepted suggestion. The inflow is freed for other suggestions.
Marks a pending transfer suggestion as rejected. Returns 404 if not found, 409 if already actioned.

requestBody.name: notes
requestBody.description: Optional notes for rejecting the suggestion

entries.description: Returns all stable user accounts for the authenticated user. These survive Plaid re-links and provide consistent references for querying transactions.
Retrieves a specific user account by ID. Returns 404 if not found or not owned by the user.
Updates customization fields (nickname, color, icon, emoji, display order, hidden status) for a user account. Only provided fields are updated.

entries.summary: Set household share visibility for a user account
entries.description: Toggles whether this account is included in the household aggregate seen by other members. Active-member-only; the caller must own the account. Returns 404 if the caller is not an active member of a household, 403 if the account does not belong to the caller.

requestBody.name: visibility
requestBody.description: shared: included in the household aggregate. hidden: excluded, but the member stays in the household.

entries.description: Returns a machine-readable JSON export of the authenticated user's own data (GDPR Article 20, right to data portability). Scoped strictly to the caller: rows belonging to household peers are never included, and credentials, encrypted-at-rest secrets and third-party authentication identifiers are excluded.
Initiates account deletion with 30-day grace period. User will receive email with cancellation link.
Cancels a pending account deletion using the cancellation token from the email.

entries.summary: Get a verified PostHog Support identity
entries.description: Returns the authenticated Clerk subject and its server-generated HMAC for PostHog Support.
Retrieves the authenticated user's privacy settings, creating defaults if none exist.
Updates the authenticated user's privacy settings with GDPR validation.

Retrieves the authenticated user's existing profile, then attempts a best-effort last-login timestamp update. An update failure does not fail the response, and returned last_login_at is the value fetched before that update.
Updates the authenticated user's profile with validated data.
Liveness check. Returns 200 with {"status":"ok"} when critical dependencies are healthy, 503 otherwise. Carries no version, timing, or dependency detail.
Public endpoint for Paddle to send subscription and payment event notifications. Verifies HMAC-SHA256 signature, stores in database, and enqueues async processing job.
Receives and processes webhook notifications from Plaid. Validates JWT signature and stores for async processing.
